title: Channel Update - Future of the Dungeon Dive and All Fiction is Fantasy
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2OdJHlmdu3A

A short, consequential update. Daniel (@dungeondive) ends the Hobbycast — scripted, research-heavy, and despite being audio-only it took longer than his videos while never finding traction. The final episode will cover all 31 horror films he watched in October.

Fridays are repurposed to solo RPGs, a decision made on analytics: "solo RPG" keeps surfacing as a search term, so he leans into it with actual plays, discussions, and occasional community hangout topics seeded through Patreon.

The headline is the split. Book content moves to a second channel, *All Fiction is Fantasy*, because YouTube does not like multi-topic channels and he cannot rely on Patreon alone to pay the bills. Old book videos stay on The Dungeon Dive but are being compiled by subject into supercuts on the new channel — the Sword & Sorcery Saga run is already up as a four-hour video. Game-and-book crossover content stays here, since he considers that combination the thing that distinguishes him from other board game channels.

He is candid throughout about money: now working the channel three days a week alongside another job, patrons lost over the past two months, and a solo RPG beginner's guide he'd hoped would go viral and didn't. He also admits he dislikes self-promotion and knows he should be better at it.

----

Was splitting the channel the right call, or does the algorithm punish exactly the range that made the channel worth following?
